#5651. Industrial automation startup Path Robotics raises $300M in funding

Path Robotics Inc., a startup working to automate industrial welding workflows, today announced that it has raised $300 million in funding.

Georgian led the Series E round. It was joined by a consortium that included the venture capital arms of Yamaha Motor Co. and Navier Corp., one of South Korea’s largest tech firms. The investment gives Path Robotics a post-money valuation of $2.45 billion.

Welding tasks were historically difficult to automate because of a phenomenon called heat-induced metal distortion. It occurs when the heat produced by a welding torch warps the metal parts being joined together. Furthermore, the parts change shape again when they cool down. Those distortions are often unpredictable, which means they can throw off a robot arm that follows a static, pre-programmed welding plan.

There are also other sources of complexity. Mass produced metal parts that are based on the same blueprint often differ slightly because of manufacturing inconsistencies. In many cases, those variations make it necessary to adjust the way welding is performed. That isn’t always possible with traditional automation software.

Path Robotics has developed an AI model that addresses those challenges. Obsidian, as it’s called, is specifically designed to power industrial robots equipped with welding torches. The company says that the model can observe how metal parts change shape during the welding process and adjust its workflow accordingly. Furthermore, it automatically accounts for unexpected part variations.

Obsidian monitors the welding workflow using four lasers attached to the torch that it controls. The emitters illuminate the parts being welded together and the reflected light is captured by a pair of cameras. According to Path Robotics, Obsidian collects data not only during the welding process but also before and after each run.

The data powers an AI model that the company refers to as a weld world model. Path Robotics’ researchers use it to generate simulated welding projects. Those simulations, in turn, power Obsidian’s training workflow.

Path Robotics originally developed Obsidian for large robotic workstations called welding cells. In April, it introduced a four-legged robot called Rove that uses the model to automate shipbuilding tasks. The company says its software can also be used to make parts for vehicles, power generators, utility poles and other heavy equipment.

“We’re seeing accelerating demand from manufacturers that need to expand production capacity but can’t get there with traditional automation,” said Path Robotics co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Andy Lonsberry. “This capital allows us to scale our welding business alongside our customers while investing further in the data, compute, and model development needed to take on every task before and after welding.”

#5650. MIT scientists turn immune cells into cancer killers inside the body

MIT researchers have developed a new technique that allows them to transform immune cells into cancer fighters directly inside the body, potentially making advanced treatments for cancer and autoimmune diseases much easier to produce and administer.

The method focuses on natural killer (NK) cells, a type of immune cell that can be engineered to recognize and destroy harmful cells. These include cancerous T cells and T cells that mistakenly attack healthy tissue, contributing to conditions such as lymphoma and autoimmune hepatitis.

Rather than extracting immune cells from a patient and modifying them in a laboratory, the researchers use tiny particles made of fatty molecules to deliver genetic instructions directly to NK cells. These instructions, carried by messenger RNA, tell the cells to produce specialized proteins that help them identify and eliminate diseased T cells.

The resulting cells, known as CAR NK cells, could eventually be used against several different diseases. By carrying out the engineering process inside the body, the new approach could eliminate much of the time, expense, and complexity involved in manufacturing personalized immune cell therapies.

"The manufacturing challenges with CAR NK cells are significant. The idea here is you can deliver a nanoparticle that will modify your own NK cells with a CAR construct and teach them to attack tumor cells," says Daniel Anderson, a professor in MIT's Department of Chemical Engineering and a member of MIT's Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research and Institute for Medical Engineering and Science.

Anderson is the senior author of the research, published in Nature Biotechnology. The lead authors are MIT postdoctoral researcher Yuang Chen and graduate students Julia Monkovic and Haseeb Mughal. Robert Langer, MIT's David H. Koch Institute Professor, also contributed to the study.

Why Current Cancer Immunotherapies Are So Complex

Immune cell engineering has already transformed treatment options for certain cancers. During the past decade, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved seven cancer therapies that use genetically modified T cells, known as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells.

These treatments work by equipping T cells with specially designed receptors that recognize particular markers, or antigens, on other cells. When an engineered T cell encounters its designated target, such as a protein associated with cancer, it becomes activated and attacks the cell carrying that marker.

CAR T cell therapies have been especially effective against blood cancers arising from B cells. These include certain forms of leukemia and lymphoma, as well as multiple myeloma.

However, preparing these treatments involves several complicated steps. Doctors first collect blood from the patient and send it to a specialized facility. There, technicians separate the T cells, genetically modify them to produce the desired receptors, and grow enough engineered cells for treatment. The finished cells must then be transported back to the hospital and infused into the patient.

Natural Killer Cells Offer a Different Way to Fight Cancer

Scientists have recently been exploring whether natural killer cells could be engineered in a similar way. One important advantage is their potential to treat cancers and autoimmune conditions involving abnormal T cells.

Trying to use CAR T cells against diseased T cells creates a major problem. Because both the engineered cells and their intended targets are T cells, the modified cells may recognize and destroy one another. This unintended attack can undermine the treatment.

Natural killer cells avoid this complication because they are a different type of immune cell. They can be programmed to attack harmful T cells without triggering the same problem of engineered T cells killing each other.

"NK cells can treat these T cell malignancies -- not only T cell cancer, but also T cell autoimmune diseases," Chen says.

Producing CAR NK cells outside the body, however, still requires much of the specialized equipment, labor, and processing associated with CAR T cell manufacturing. To overcome these limitations, the MIT team investigated whether NK cells could instead be engineered "in vivo," meaning directly inside the body.

"If a patient can just get an infusion of nanoparticles, it would dramatically simplify the process and reduce costs," Anderson says.

Although researchers are actively developing CAR NK cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune disorders, none have received FDA approval.

How mRNA Nanoparticles Reprogram Immune Cells

The MIT team designed lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) capable of transporting messenger RNA into natural killer cells. The mRNA carries instructions for producing a chimeric antigen receptor that directs the modified immune cell toward a specific target.

The technology can be adapted to recognize different proteins depending on the disease being treated. For example, the researchers can provide instructions for a receptor that recognizes CD19, a protein found on B cells, or CD3, a protein present on T cells, including those responsible for autoimmune attacks.

To help the nanoparticles reach the correct immune cells, the scientists covered their surfaces with antibody fragments. These fragments recognize and attach to receptors on NK cells, helping deliver the genetic instructions where they are needed.

Once inside an NK cell, the mRNA directs the production of the new receptor, giving the immune cell the ability to recognize and attack its intended target.

The researchers then tested whether this approach could efficiently reprogram NK cells and whether the resulting cells could combat cancer and autoimmune disease in mice.

Reprogrammed Immune Cells Eliminate Tumors in Mice

The initial experiments produced encouraging results. After injecting the nanoparticles into mice, the researchers successfully modified approximately 80 percent of the NK cells they were targeting.

They next investigated whether these engineered cells could attack tumors. In mice with an aggressive form of melanoma, three of the five animals treated with nanoparticles designed to direct NK cells against the cancer experienced complete remission.

The researchers also tested the technique against T cell lymphoma using humanized mice. These animals receive transfusions of human blood cells, temporarily giving them immune systems that share certain characteristics with those of humans.

In this model, the treatment produced substantial tumor destruction. After five injections of the nanoparticles, the tumors were completely eliminated.

Importantly, these results were comparable to those achieved with CAR NK cells produced through the more traditional method of collecting NK cells, modifying them outside the body, and then returning them to the animals.

This suggests that generating CAR NK cells directly inside the body could offer similar cancer-fighting capabilities while avoiding the complicated manufacturing process required by conventional cell therapies.

A Single Injection Reverses Autoimmune Liver Damage

The researchers also wanted to determine whether their technology could help treat autoimmune diseases, in which the immune system mistakenly damages healthy tissues.

They focused on autoimmune hepatitis, a condition in which abnormal T cells attack hepatocytes, the main functional cells of the liver. By designing nanoparticles that instruct NK cells to recognize these harmful T cells, the scientists tested whether they could interrupt the autoimmune response.

The treatment successfully eliminated the autoreactive T cells in mice with the disease. Even more encouragingly, the animals' damaged liver tissue healed after the harmful immune cells were removed.

These improvements occurred after just one nanoparticle injection, demonstrating the potential of the approach beyond cancer treatment.

"This study is an excellent example of the power of nano delivery systems and their ability to potentially treat cancer and other diseases," Langer says.

A New Direction for Cancer and Autoimmune Treatments

The researchers believe that reprogramming natural killer cells inside the body could eventually provide new treatment options for a much wider range of conditions.

Among the diseases they hope to target are multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis, both of which can involve harmful immune responses driven by dysfunctional T cells.

Although the findings are promising, the experiments were conducted in mice, and further research will be necessary to determine whether the technique is safe and effective in humans.

If successful, the technology could make engineered immune cell treatments considerably more accessible by replacing a lengthy laboratory manufacturing process with the direct delivery of genetic instructions through nanoparticles.

The research received funding from Sanofi, the Marble Center for Cancer Nanomedicine, and a Koch Institute Support (core) Grant from the National Cancer Institute.

#5649. Mastering Digital Marketing - How to Grow Your Business Online

Having a solid digital marketing strategy is essential if you want to succeed as a business owner in the modern day. Effective digital marketing lets you get more eyes on your business and ensure consistent growth.

Because digital marketing trends are forever changing, it’s important to stay on top of your brand’s strategy. Doing so ensures that you stand out above your competitors and gain the recognition that your brand deserves.

If you’re unsure how to master your digital marketing strategy, consider working with an expert company that can help you figure out which direction to go. A professional agency, such as Scorpion Digital Marketing Agency, can support your online efforts to maximize your success.

If you don’t want to outsource your digital marketing processes, try these top tips below to maintain an effective digital marketing strategy and boost your business growth.

Your website is where most of your new audience will find your business and your existing customers will shop for your new products and services. If you create a strong first impression through your website, you can gain credibility and authority in your industry.

Make sure to regularly update your website content so it’s accurate and on-trend. Doing so also signals to Google that your website is authoritative and credible, increasing your rankings on search engine results pages (SERPs).

The higher your rankings, the higher your visibility, meaning you can expand your reach with minimal effort. When updating your content, use plenty of industry-relevant keywords and key phrases to ensure your target audience finds your site.

With a strong social media strategy, you can significantly expand your reach and gain recognition as a trustworthy brand. Regularly posting content enables you to provide consistent value to your audience while displaying your expertise.

You can create posts highlighting the benefits of your products or the quality of your services. You can share positive testimonials and reviews from happy customers to build your credibility.

Social media platforms allow you to connect directly with your target audience too. You can answer queries and concerns in your DMs and show the human side of your brand.

Video marketing is becoming increasingly effective. Over four-fifths of consumer internet traffic comes from videos, so it's the perfect way to expand your reach and drive more traffic to your website.

Whether you use live or pre-filmed video content, you can capture your target audience's attention and provide helpful information in an engaging way. You can share demonstrations of how to use your products or explain your services in more detail to persuade consumers to check out your brand.

#5648. Mortgage Demand Jumps 6.2% as Rates Fall for Fourth Straight Week

Mortgage applications rose last week, as interest rates decreased for the fourth week in a row, hitting their lowest levels since mid-September, as a positive jobs report and the results of the midterm election bolster the outlook.

For the week ending Nov. 6 the Mortgage Bankers Association's Market Composite Index—a measure of total mortgage loan application volume—increased 6.2% on a seasonally adjusted basis from one week earlier.

The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of mortgage applications to purchase a single-family home, increased 8% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment. Purchase applications were down 18% from a year ago.

According to MBA calculations, the average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages with conforming loan balances is 7.21%, a slight decrease from last week's rate of 7.3%. Rates averaged 5.99% a year ago.

Mortgage rates dropped to 7.18% last week from 7.21% the week before, according to a separate survey from Freddie Mac.

“Mortgage rates declined for the fourth straight week,” said Joel Kan, MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist. “The declining trend in rates helped to spur stronger application activity, although the pace of purchase and refinance applications remain considerably lower than a year ago."

In recent weeks, high interest rates had pushed more buyers toward riskier Adjustable Rate Mortgages. However, this past week, ARM applications decreased to 10.9% of the total. applications, down from 11.4% the previous week.

FHA and VA loans saw "particularly strong growth" this past week, said Kan.

The share of FHA loan applications decreased to 15.5% from 16% the prior week. The VA share of total applications increased to 12% from 11.2% the prior week. And the USDA share of total applications decreased to 0.5% from 0.6% the week prior.

The refinance share of mortgage activity remained unchanged at 39.8%, but was 57% lower than the same week one year ago, as homeowners remain locked into their lower interest rates.

October's positive jobs report, which showed that the U.S. economy added 165,000 nonfarm jobs in October, has increased the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates when it next meets in December.

CME Group's FedWatch has the likelihood of an additional rate hike at around 77%.

The positive jobs report news was compounded by broad Democrat wins in the midterm elections. Democrats, many of whom ran on a message of affordability, won the majority in both the House and the Senate. Voters aged 18 to 34 and men aged 18 to 49 had ranked housing costs as a top political issue in a rcent CNBC survey.

Trump's former Federal Housing Commissioner Frank Cassidy called the midterms a "wake-up call."

"Everyone needs to get serious about tackling and addressing housing affordability. It can't be ignored anymore," he told Realtor.com®.

Mortgage rates are calculated based on various factors in the economy, and the length of your loan and credit score will also factor into the mortgage rate you qualify for.

That makes the duration on the loans roughly comparable, and mortgage lenders use the 10-year Treasury as a benchmark for setting rates, adding on a risk premium.

Long-term yields for Treasury notes are determined by a number of factors, including the supply of and demand for U.S. government debt, and investor expectations for inflation over the life of the bonds.

#5647. IBM Quantum announces upcoming Nighthawk r3 processor designed to execute 10,000 operations

IBM Corp. today announced the Quantum Nighthawk r3, its next-generation processor designed to tackle larger, more complex computations at high speed while maintaining quality.

The company also said that in 2027, IBM plans to link two r3 quantum processors into a single system capable of running up to 10,000 quantum operations, scaling to more than 1,000 qubits between them.

“Useful quantum computing hinges on whether results can be delivered with accuracy and speed, both are fundamental,” said Director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta. “IBM Nighthawk is already showing us what that looks like today.”

The new r3 chip follows the introduction of Nighthawk r2 in September, which supports more than 7,500 quantum operations on 120 qubits.

Qubits are the fundamental unit of logical information in a quantum computer, similar to a classical computer’s bit. Unlike classical bits, which can be a 0 or 1, qubits can be 0, 1 or a “superposition” of both at the same time. Using this property, quantum processors such as IBM’s Nighthawk can do rapid, complex parallel calculations.

The r2 chip introduced a groundbreaking high-speed qubit reset architecture that lets developers and researchers quickly prime qubits after measurements. Under normal circumstances, after a quantum circuit runs and the result is measured, the qubits must return to the ground state before the next program can run; this process can take hundreds of milliseconds, meaning the chip remains idle during that time. With the new technology, this wait period can be reduced from about 200 milliseconds down to roughly 25 nanoseconds without disturbing neighboring qubits.

Building on lessons learned from Nighthawk r2 and the technology built into it, IBM said r3 will extend the same high-speed architecture to larger quantum systems to support 10,000 operations on 520 programmable qubits with 2,034 physical quantum components.

A physical qubit is the actual, hardware-level quantum device that stores the quantum information. In Nighthawk, the qubits are superconducting and arranged in a square lattice. The programmable qubits are the measurable, active quantum data units, while additional quantum components support them, including couplers and reset elements.

IBM said it has already demonstrated two critical technologies that will make combining two r3 chips. This year, the company connected two Nighthawk r1 processors using four l-couplers, or “long-range” quantum interconnects. These act as a physical bridge between separate processors to create a larger machine.

In the demonstration, the couplers achieved a 99.4% transfer fidelity, progressing towards the target of 99.9% fidelity. The company also connected cryogenic modules into a single system.

In 2027, IBM intends to progress using these modularity advances to scale Nighthawk into a larger quantum system. By connecting two Nighthawk r3 processors into a single 1,040 system, IBM will extend this high-performance architecture to tackle larger and more complex computations.

“As we scale this architecture to larger and more powerful quantum computers, the capabilities of quantum computation will reach new levels as we integrate more closely with classical resources and march ahead to fault tolerance,” added Gambetta.

IBM also announced that its cloud-based service for researchers and developers, IBM Quantum Platform, will bring high-performance classical and quantum computing together in a single managed environment.

Users can now integrate quantum workflows directly with HPC and classical resources on the platform, or with classical compute on their laptop or any number of the world’s most powerful supercomputers.

Integrating quantum and classical computing permits traditional computers to orchestrate algorithms and computations on specialized central processing units and graphics processing units, while the quantum computer runs parallel computations. Users are already seeing promising results, including Cleveland Clinic using the platform to process 2.6 million samples up to three times faster to model biological structures.

Direct integration of quantum and classical systems will also help drive breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Error correction is fundamental to handling the noise that can destabilize individual qubits, creating a high chance of errors rising out of computations. Quantum Platform is launching pulse-level access to give researchers precise control over how they can detect, understand and correct errors within quantum and classical architectures.

IBM recently launched a new quantum error-correction platform that addresses this, in collaboration with Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The build physically colocates Nighthawk processors with next-generation AMD GPUs and CPUs.

#5645. Red Hat accelerates agentic adoption across hybrid environments

Enterprise ambitions for artificial intelligence are outpacing the infrastructure and budgets needed to support them. Red Hat AI faces a familiar enterprise challenge: turning ambitious plans for artificial intelligence into production deployments that deliver measurable returns.

Organizations must also decide how to deploy and manage increasingly complex AI workloads across existing infrastructure without letting costs spiral. At Red Hat Summit 2026 in May, Red Hat Inc. outlined its approach to those challenges through expanded platform capabilities, automation and an open-source development process that relies on community contributions.

“I think everybody here loves that because that does lead to sovereignty as well,” said Rob Strechay, principal analyst at theCUBE, during the event. “They’re actually building on top of open source and enhancing it in a way that provides more value in supporting it, which is key to their success.”

This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s ongoing coverage of the AWS Financial Services Symposium. (* Disclosure below.)

Deploying and managing AI workloads across hybrid cloud environments presents new operational challenges for enterprises. Red Hat’s answer is Red Hat AI 3.4, an updated version of its enterprise AI platform that supports agentic AI deployments and large-scale inference across hybrid environments.

The company also announced two new managed services: Red Hat AI Inference and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization Service on IBM Cloud. Red Hat AI Inference is designed to integrate real-time AI inference directly into clients’ production workflows, while OpenShift Virtualization enables clients to migrate and run virtual machines at scale. Both services are intended to accelerate hybrid cloud adoption.

“What’s really going to drive inference demand exponentially is AI agents,” said Joe Fernandes, vice president and general manager of Red Hat AI. “We provide a platform where customers can deploy and manage their AI agents across a hybrid infrastructure environment.”

The next piece of Red Hat’s agentic strategy comes in the form of Ansible Automation Platform 2.7, which connects AI-generated insights to governed infrastructure actions. Its self-service automation capabilities allow authorized users in locations such as branch offices and factory floors to manage servers and networks within established controls.

“Customers are now able to use their own data to calculate savings and efficiencies,” said Sathish Balakrishnan, vice president and general manager of Red Hat’s Ansible business unit. “Every action, whether it’s triggered by humans, an event or an AI agent, passes through the same [access controls], approval gates, audit trails, content signing and credential management.”

AI budgets are booming: according to theCUBE Research, Analysts project that AI cloud spending could approach $2.5 trillion by 2026, growing at roughly 44% year-over-year. However, that investment does not always return concrete value. Research shows that 50.7% of organizations rely on public AI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot but only 20.2% report enterprise-wide AI deployments built on a governed framework.

“Most people are token consumers and that is part of the reason they’re trying to figure out how do they get to production,” Strechay said. “How do they get out of these death-by-pilot situations and become token producers so that they can offset the cost or at least lower the cost so they can get to the [return on AI investment] of those applications? You can use [OpenShift] infrastructure along with things like vLLM and some of the other things in Red Hat AI to get and become efficient in how you produce your tokens.”

Part of Red Hat’s strategy for helping customers manage sprawling AI budgets is its partnership with Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Together, AMD and Red Hat are encouraging enterprises to rethink the financials of AI. Rather than opting for the newest, most expensive hardware, clients might have better results if matching compute resources to the workload, according to John Hampton, corporate vice president of global enterprise technical sales at AMD.

“So many of these enterprises just ran out and bought big [graphics processing unit] clusters because they knew they had to solve for AI,” he said. “Enterprises are coming to us and saying, ‘This is exploding. It’s good that we’re using AI, but we can’t afford this anymore.’”

Red Hat has also joined forces with Intel Corp. to help customers determine which combination of hardware and software best suits their workloads. As enterprises look to reduce inference costs, the companies are emphasizing the value of choosing the right mix of CPUs and GPUs rather than relying on a single approach.

“As we’ve gone through this with our customers in the industry, we’ve seen that people often have just assumed, ‘I’ve got a hammer. I need the nail to hit it with,’” said Bill Pearson, vice president of data center and AI at Intel. “Once they take a step back to say, ‘Wait a minute. I have these [central processing units] in my data center’ or ‘I need to figure out how to balance the right number of CPUs with the right number of GPUs to achieve that outcome I’m looking for,’ they’re actually going to get better results at a better price point for delivering lower-cost tokens.”

Red Hat announced several collaborations at the summit, including Red Hat AI Factory with Nvidia Corp. The partnership includes support for Nvidia’s Blackwell architecture and upcoming Vera Rubin platform, as well as participation in Nvidia’s OpenShell project for AI agent sandboxing and secure execution.

“Moving AI from corporate experimentation to an industrial engine requires a sovereign, consistent foundation across the hybrid cloud,” said Chris Wright, chief technology officer and senior vice president for global engineering at Red Hat, in the announcement. “Through our strategic co-engineering efforts with Nvidia, Red Hat provides the architectural control and open source innovation enterprises need to scale agentic AI with confidence.”

Red Hat’s other partnership announcements focused on agentic AI and edge computing. Boomi LP, which brands itself as a data activation company, is collaborating with Red Hat on a single, integrated stack for deploying agentic AI at scale. The partnerships with Panasonic Connect and Voyager cover edge computing solutions and space edge micro data centers, respectively.

Red Hat’s expanding ecosystem of partnerships reflects the growing range of enterprise applications for agentic AI. The challenge for organizations is determining how those capabilities can address their specific business needs, according to Matt Hicks, president and chief executive officer of Red Hat.

“From the board level down … you have a feeling of, ‘We have to be able to harness what this technology can do,’” said Matt Hicks. “The people that will be the most successful with AI are the people that have the most questions. People that know business, they know their domain. Those are the ones [that] have no barriers to what they can do and change. It’s just about getting started.”

Sovereign AI has become an increasingly important consideration for enterprises seeking greater control over their data and infrastructure. Gartner Inc. forecasts that the sovereign cloud infrastructure-as-a-service market will grow at a compound annual rate of 36% through 2028.

Red Hat is expanding support for sovereign cloud while allowing customers to keep the infrastructure they already invested in. That includes collaborations with Core42, which specializes in sovereign-by-design infrastructure, and Sopra Steria, a longstanding European collaborator on sovereign AI initiatives.

Red Hat is also extending its software security capabilities as enterprises adopt agentic AI. Fedora Hummingbird Linux is a container-native operating system designed for agent-first development, with an automated software delivery pipeline. Meanwhile, Red Hat Hardened Images provides a catalog of minimal container images designed to reduce vulnerabilities and strengthen software supply-chain security.

At this point, sovereign AI and governance play an essential role in giving customers choice and control, according to Ashesh Badani, senior vice president and chief product officer of Red Hat.

“Whether an organization is meeting jurisdictional mandates or reclaiming its data from proprietary silos, we are providing the capabilities and platforms to build a more self-determined future,” he said in a Red Hat press release.

#5644. Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

In the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

When writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

Storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

In the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

Social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

To encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

An effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt users to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

Writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

#5643. Jester Lands in Court: Florida Woman Accused of Stealing Properties With Forged Deeds

A Florida woman has been accused of perpetrating a brazen deed fraud scam and illicitly transferred ownership of three properties in a scheme to fund her lavish lifestyle.

Melissa Jester, 41, of Bunnell, FL, is facing criminal charges after authorities say she forged a property owner's signature on deeds, transferred the land to a company she controlled, and pocketed the proceeds from one of the sales. She was arrested Nov. 6.

The victim, who owned three vacant lots in Florida for nearly two decades, recently discovered that the properties were transferred out of her name without her knowledge—and that one had been sold for nearly $30,000, according to the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office.

The victim contacted the authorities on Aug. 27 and said she had never authorized the sale or transfer of the properties. The three lots are located in the coastal city of Palm Coast, about 30 miles north of Daytona Beach.

An investigation was launched, and detectives uncovered what they described as a paper trail of forged documents, suspicious financial transactions, and a property sale that ultimately helped lead them to Jester.

Detectives traced a trail of forged documents and fraudulent financial transactions to Jester.

According to investigators, paperwork transferring ownership of all three lots to Florida Ohana Homes LLC, a company owned by Jester, was mailed to the Flagler County Clerk of Courts on June 29, 2026.

The paperwork appeared to have the property owner's signature on it. It was forged, investigators say.

Jester took further steps to hide her involvement by purchasing a money order on June 18 to pay the filing fees for the property under a different name, according to the affidavit.

The money order was purchased at the Amscot location on Palm Coast Parkway. The transaction did not require identification.

But the alleged scheme did not end there.

According to the Flagler County Sheriff’s Office, Jester, acting as managing member of Florida Ohana Homes LLC, then sold one of the stolen lots for $29,970 to an unsuspecting buyer on Sept. 10.

Surveillance video from the UPS Store on Belle Terre Parkway showed Jester signing the warranty deed and having it notarized. The money was transferred to the Bank of America account for Florida Ohana Homes LLC.

Authorities also allege that Jester transferred $8,000 from the business account into her personal account at VyStar Credit Union, where the money was spent on hotel stays and purchases throughout Flagler County.

By following the financial transactions, detectives were able to trace the money and recover a substantial portion of the proceeds from the alleged illicit sale.

More than $14,000 was seized from the company's Bank of America account and another $6,000 from Jester's personal credit union account. A total of $20,000 was recovered.

On Nov. 6, deputies located Jester driving in Bunnell, FL, and arrested her on charges of grand theft and obtaining property valued between $20,000 and $50,000 by swindle.

She is being held at the Sheriff Perry Hall Inmate Detention Facility on a $45,000 bond.

Flagler County Sheriff Rick Staly said the case stood out because, unlike many property fraud schemes involving suspects operating from distant locations, the alleged perpetrator lived nearby and conducted the transaction in person.

“Most of the deed fraud we see is run by scammers hiding in another state or another country. This one lived in Bunnell and signed the closing papers in front of a security camera in Palm Coast,” Sheriff Staly said. “Our detectives followed the trail of forgeries and money and recovered most of it for the victim.”

#5642. Why Builders May Be More Motivated To Sell Than Homeowners

Here’s something most homebuyers don’t think about. When the housing market slows down, homeowners and builders don’t always respond the same way.

Think about it. If you’re selling your house and aren’t getting the offers you want, you could make the choice to take it off the market and stay put, and wait for things to improve.

But builders? They may be more motivated to stay the course.

They’ve already invested money in building those houses. And every completed home that sits unsold means money tied up in a property, plus ongoing costs that can add up.

That’s why some builders may be more motivated to negotiate right now. And that could work in your favor.

You’ve probably seen the headlines. According to the latest report from the National Association of Realtors (NAR), pending home sales – homes that have gone under contract but haven’t closed yet – fell 7.3% in September and 11.3% compared to last year.

Why? Higher mortgage rates are making it harder for buyers to make the numbers work. Now, that report tracks existing homes, not new construction. But we’re seeing signs of the same slowdown on the builder side, too.

According to the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), builder confidence dropped to 29 in October, its lowest level since June 2012. Traffic from prospective buyers also dropped to its lowest level in more than a decade, excluding the start of the pandemic.

As Robert Dietz, Chief Economist at NAHB, explains:

“Demand persists, but higher mortgage rates, elevated construction costs and weaker consumer confidence are keeping more buyers on the sidelines.”

A homeowner may be able to wait for the right offer. But a builder with several finished houses sitting unsold may have more reason to get those homes sold sooner rather than later.

And that means they may be more willing to work with you than you think.

If you’ve always assumed builders don’t negotiate, take a look at what they’re actually doing. According to the latest survey from NAHB, in October:

65% of builders are offering sales incentives.

43% are cutting prices, the highest share recorded between 2020 and 2026.

And 6% is what they’re typically taking off the price.

So, yes. Builders absolutely do negotiate. And with demand slowing, there’s good reason to explore just how flexible they may be right now.

That could mean asking for a lower price. But it could also mean asking for a mortgage-rate buydown, help with closing costs, or upgrades that would otherwise cost you extra.

And here’s a tip that could make a real difference.

Don’t just look at the newest communities or the prettiest model homes. Look for builders with completed houses that haven’t sold yet.

Those are sometimes called quick move-in homes or spec homes. And the longer one of those move-in ready homes sits unsold, the more reason a builder may have to consider an offer that helps get it off their books.

Don’t assume the advertised price or incentive package is the best they’ll do.

This is where having your own agent can really pay off. An agent who knows the local market can help you compare what builders are offering, identify communities with more available homes, and understand where there’s room to negotiate.

Of course, not every builder will offer the same incentives. And some may be more flexible on closing costs or mortgage rates than on the price itself.

The trick is knowing where to look, what to ask for, and how much room there may be to negotiate. And that’s where having your own agent is key.

A homeowner who isn't ready to accept a lower offer may be able to wait. But a builder with finished houses to sell has a different set of priorities. And that could work in your favor.If you're ready to buy, talk to a local agent about which builders have completed homes sitting on the market in your area see what they're willing to offer to get them sold.

#5641. Agents may soon be the main workload, and most of the time they’re doing nothing

As AI agents take on more enterprise work, agent sandboxing has become a basic requirement rather than an afterthought. Every agent that writes code, runs tools or drives a browser needs hard walls around it. Those walls also can’t come at the cost of runaway compute bills.

Google LLC’s answer is Agent Substrate, an open-source project built on Kubernetes that the company donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation alongside its gVisor sandbox. Customers have raised the same problem for the past 18 months: They need to run agentic workloads securely and efficiently on the infrastructure they already have, according to Brandon Royal (pictured, left), product manager, AI agents and infrastructure, at Google Cloud.

“Any agent needs to be fully isolated,” Royal said. “Whether it’s accessing tools or using a computer or a browser, there needs to be some level of isolation, period, full stop.”

Royal and Benjamin Elder (right), staff software engineer at Google, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how agent sandboxing is central to Google’s open-source Agent Substrate. (* Disclosure below.)

Agent Substrate starts with hardened sandbox runtimes densely packed on Kubernetes clusters. All traffic passes through a layer that applies policy and understands identity, so an agent can reach nothing it hasn’t been explicitly granted, Elder explained. The project also keeps secrets out of the agent’s hands by injecting credentials on the wire.

“Don’t expose credentials to the sandbox,” Elder said. “Don’t let the agent touch the credentials. Instead, when it requests to do something, you can make a decision about outside the sandbox.”

Security is only half the equation. Agents in a swarm spend much of their time blocked, waiting on a large language model call or on a human to follow up. Agent Substrate snapshots those idle agents out of memory and CPU, stores them offline and restores them when they’re needed, freeing resources across the cluster, according to Elder.

“Should you be holding compute while you’re getting coffee? Because you might come back in five minutes. You might come back in five hours or five days,” Royal said. “We don’t know.”

Google is already building on the project. Gemini Managed Agents now runs on Agent Substrate and gets the same density, efficiency and security guarantees, Royal noted. Google Cloud also recently introduced Agent Compute Engine to host AI agents.

“Agents are going to become the predominant workload in the future,” Royal said. “Maybe it’s six months, maybe it’s 12 months, but we see this as a really big area of growth.”

#5640. Who’s Buying Homes with Cash Right Now?

Ryan Serhant, CEO of SERHANT, says there isn’t just 1 housing market right now. There are really 4: cash buyers, buyers who need a mortgage, homeowners with low mortgage rates, and builders.

Today, let’s zoom in on the 1st group – cash buyers.

According to the National Association of Realtors (NAR), 27% of homes sold in September were bought with all cash. That’s more than 1 in 4 buyers. And that’s a pretty big number, especially when so many people are struggling with affordability.

So where is all that cash coming from? When you hear a number like that, it’s easy to picture wealthy investors buying up houses left and right. But that’s not necessarily the case. Some of those cash buyers are actually homeowners who’ve built up enough equity to buy their next home outright.

Here’s what you should know about who’s paying cash and what that really means for the market.

Cash buyers tend to fall into a few groups, according to NAR:

Homeowners who sold a house and are using that money to buy their next one

So, it’s not all those big investors social media talks about. That 1st group may include people a lot more like you. Here’s how. According to Cotality, the average homeowner with a mortgage has about $310,000 in equity.

That’s a big deal right now. Many homeowners feel stuck because they don’t want to give up the low mortgage rate they have today. But once they learn they may have enough equity to move and pay cash for their next home, today’s rates don’t matter nearly as much. Because buying in all cash means…

No need to borrow at today’s mortgage rates

No loan approval process, so you may be able to close faster

And even if the equity won’t cover the whole purchase, putting more of it toward the next home means borrowing less. That can mean a smaller monthly payment, too.

But cash buyers like this are more common in some places than others. And how big of a segment of your local market this is, is going to depend on where you live.

For example, Realtor.com data shows cash buyers made up almost 47% of sales in Mississippi and 46% in Montana earlier this year (see map below).

According to Realtor.com, the states with the most cash buyers reflect “a mix of affordability, wealth and buyer demographics.” Think places with lower home prices, or lots of retirees and 2nd-home buyers.

So, depending on where you live, you may see a lot more (or a lot fewer) cash buyers than the national number suggests. An agent who knows your area can tell you who’s actually buying near you.

And if all of this has you thinking everyone’s paying cash, they’re not. If you’re planning to buy and need a mortgage, you’re actually in the majority.

Based on NAR’s numbers, nearly 3 out of 4 home purchases still involve financing. And for homes priced between $200,000 and $750,000, only about 1 in 5 sold for cash, according to Realtor.com (see graph below):

That means most people buying in that price range are financing their purchase, too. So, there’s no need to assume you’re at a disadvantage just because you’re using a loan.

So, what does all this mean for you? Maybe more than you think.

If you already own a house, you may have enough equity to make your next move more affordable than you realize. And if you’re buying with a mortgage, remember, you’re in good company. Most buyers are financing their purchases, too.

The takeaway? Don’t make assumptions about what’s possible based on how other people are buying homes. What really matters is your equity, your budget, and what’s happening in your local market.

Cash buyers are a meaningful part of today’s market, but they aren’t the whole market.Whether you’re hoping to put your equity to work or you’re buying with a mortgage, a local real estate agent can help you see how much equity you have, who’s buying in your area, and what that means for your next move.

Cash buyers are a meaningful part of today’s market, but they aren’t the whole market.

Whether you’re hoping to put your equity to work or you’re buying with a mortgage, a local real estate agent can help you see how much equity you have, who’s buying in your area, and what that means for your next move.

#5639. Don't Let the Fear of a Buyer Backing Out Scare You Away from Selling

There’s nothing quite like the excitement of getting an offer on your house. You’re one step closer to moving on to what’s next. But what happens if that buyer backs out or ghosts you before closing?

If you’ve been seeing headlines about more home sales falling through lately, that possibility may be keeping you up at night. And it’s true. According to Redfin and Cotality, canceled contracts have been on the rise.

But here’s what those headlines don’t always tell you…

Most sales still go through. Only 10-15% hit this snag. And even so, there are things you can do to help keep your sale from becoming one of them.

The key is knowing what tends to scare buyers away and getting ahead of those issues before they have a chance to derail your move.

Today’s buyers are being more cautious. Mortgage rates are stretching budgets, and with more homes to choose from, buyers have more freedom to walk away if something doesn’t feel right. As Redfin explains:

“That gives house hunters more options and makes them more likely to walk away if an inspection uncovers problems, an appraisal comes in low or the seller doesn’t agree to concessions.”

That’s why an accepted offer isn’t always a guaranteed sale. But it doesn’t mean you should be afraid to put your house on the market, either.

It just means getting ahead of potential problems matters more than ever.

A Redfin survey asked real estate agents why some buyers are backing out. And their answers give you a short of cheatsheet into what could go sideways and how you can get ahead of those headaches (see graph below):

This is the big one. And the good news? It’s also one of the areas where you can be the most proactive.

One simple way to head this off is by getting a pre-listing inspection before your house goes on the market. That way, if something needs attention, you can decide whether to fix it upfront (before you sell), adjust your price, or disclose it and come in already prepared for what’s likely to pop up in negotiations. It’s a lot better to find the skeletons in the closet before a buyer does.

Even buyers who are pre-approved can run into financing issues before closing. And with mortgage rates putting extra pressure on affordability, some buyers are finding it harder to make the numbers work.

While you can’t control whether a buyer’s loan goes through, you can work with your agent to look closely at their financing before accepting an offer. And if affordability is the concern, your agent can help you explore whether incentives like closing cost credits or a mortgage-rate buydown could make a difference.

Sometimes, your buyer needs to sell their house before they can buy yours. And if their sale falls through, yours could be affected too.

That’s why it’s important to understand any home-sale contingencies before accepting an offer. Your agent can help you look at where the buyer is in their own selling process and what protections you may want in place.

The goal isn’t to eliminate every possible risk. It’s to avoid being caught off guard by the ones you can plan for.

Just remember when you read headlines about canceled deals, they don’t give you the full picture. Most home sales still make it to closing.

And if a sale does fall through, that doesn’t automatically mean your house won’t sell. Sometimes a buyer’s circumstances change. Sometimes an issue comes up that can be addressed before the next offer.

What matters is having an agent who knows how to spot potential problems early, help you navigate negotiations, and keep your sale moving forward.

Because while you can’t control every twist and turn, you can control how prepared you are.

There's no need to let the fear of a buyer backing out hold you back. While no sale comes with guarantees, a little preparation upfront can go a long way toward making the whole process smoother.If you're ready to make a move, talk to a local agent about whether a pre-listing inspection makes sense for you.

#5638. AI agents carry memory and storage like people, so their data needs guarding while in use

As AI agents move into production on Kubernetes, cloud engineering teams at financial companies face a security problem that encryption alone can’t solve. Container orchestration has become the default foundation for AI workloads, and the data those agents use is now the main target.

Payment networks feel that pressure more than most because every transaction carries customer data and regulatory exposure. Protecting data while it is being processed, and not just while it is stored or moving, has become central to running agents at scale, according to Krishna Mayuram (pictured), senior principal engineer and vice president of cloud engineering at Mastercard Inc.

“What we call confidential computing is when you are launching these applications in a highly secure, virtualized secure environments or confidential environments or confidential containers, you are able to protect the data in use,” Mayuram said. “We have protected data at rest, data in motion. Now, what is happening to the data in use?”

Mayuram spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cloud engineering, security problems and the challenges of protecting data in use. (* Disclosure below.)

Mastercard runs its platforms on Red Hat Inc.’s OpenShift, a Kubernetes platform that Red Hat is extending to support AI agents. Red Hat has also brought confidential containers to OpenShift on bare metal. Agents act much like microservices and need the same elastic infrastructure, Mayuram explained.

“We need to scale the platform, that’s Kubernetes which gives horizontal scaling, vertical scaling, if you will, and also the agents, just like applications, require all the elastic capabilities of Kubernetes,” Mayuram said.

Scale increases the risk, especially for a company that operates under many countries’ laws. Mastercard recently added trust services for agentic commerce. Internally, the same idea applies, with guardrails at every step from development to deployment, according to Mayuram.

“The business is distributed, the industry is very distributed, and we have different laws of the land. So all these things need to be encompassed with guardrails,” Mayuram said. “Whether agents or regular, the guardrails remain the same. The enterprise security remains same.”

#5636. Credit Scoring Is Changing: 3 Things Homebuyers Should Know

Quick, what credit score do you need to buy a home? If a number pops into your head, there’s a pretty good chance it’s wrong. And the right answer is getting harder to pin down, because the way credit scores are determined and delivered is changing – for the better.

Here’s what you need to know in today’s changing credit climate.

Fannie Mae has been tracking consumer perceptions about mortgage requirements since 2015 and found that consumers consistently overestimated the minimum credit score lenders required to qualify for a mortgage. As recently as 2023, the average guess was 652.

In reality, the long-standing benchmark for loans backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is lower, at 620, and today even that isn’t a hard rule for every mortgage they back.

Like the Fannie Mae research, a recent survey from Veterans United found consumers continue to overestimate what it takes to qualify for a home loan:

The takeaway? Guessing wrong can cost you.

A renter who assumes their score is too low and they can’t qualify for a mortgage may never take steps to find out for sure.

For decades, the mortgage industry relied on one set of scores – Classic FICO. Thanks to a push to promote competition, make credit scoring more inclusive, and help more Americans become homeowners, the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) has approved the use of new credit score models such as FICO 10T and VantageScore 4.0.

A different model can mean a different number for the same person. VantageScore says its model can score about 33 million adults that the Classic FICO’s model can’t. So the score you saw on an app last month may not be the one your lender pulls.

Remember: the models may be new, but the basics haven’t changed.

Your credit score is important – no matter how it’s measured. Following the same basic rules will benefit your profile in the old and new score models:

Because while credit models may change, the general advice for you to improve your score doesn’t. Financial awareness and consistency mixed with a little willpower can go a long way.

Don't make credit or homebuying decisions from a chart, an app, or a friend's advice. With the rules shifting and so many misconceptions out there, it's never too early to talk to a professional loan officer for advice on credit, budgeting, and what it would take to qualify for a mortgage.You may be closer to owning a home than you think.

#5635. The Home Insurance Move That Could Save You $440 a Year

When you’re planning a move, every monthly cost counts. That’s why it can be frustrating to see home insurance keep creeping up. According to Intercontinental Exchange, it now makes up 9.6% of the average monthly mortgage payment.

But the latest numbers show some progress on that front – as the increases start to slow down. Here’s what you need to know and what you can do about it.

A look at the past two years shows how much things have cooled down. In mid-2024, home insurance premiums rose 4.3% in a single quarter. By the second quarter of this year, that was down to 1.8%. That’s the smallest quarterly growth in almost 3 years – and that’s a good thing (see graph below):

As Andy Walden, Head of Mortgage and Housing Market Research at Intercontinental Exchange, explains:

“Property insurance has been a fast-growing component of the monthly mortgage payment, but this quarter’s data shows the pace of increase is finally slowing.”

While your premium will likely still go up over time, it may not climb as quickly as it did a couple of years ago. And that’s, at the very least, a step in the right direction.

Here’s where you have some say in what you pay. Let’s take current homeowners as an example. Intercontinental Exchange found that when homeowners shopped around and switched insurance companies, their premiums went down 6.6% on average. Those who stayed with their current company saw an increase of 10.4% (see graph below):

Think about that. That’s a big difference and it goes to show that looking for a new provider can literally pay off.

That works out to about $440 a year in savings for the people who switched. And they didn’t have to give up coverage to get it. Their deductibles dipped 1.4%, and their coverage limits actually rose 7.3%.

While this example is current homeowners, the same general idea applies for first-time buyers too. Shop around and get multiple quotes before you pick your insurance provider. Then, once you’re settled in, review your policy each year when it comes up for renewal. You’re not locked into the first price you get.

The home itself plays a role as well. According to John Burns Research and Consulting (JBREC), newly built homes are 10% to 15% less expensive to insure than older ones nationally.

And while a brand-new home won’t necessarily be the right fit for every buyer, if you’re open to one, it could be one more way to keep your monthly insurance costs down.

Home insurance is certainly a bigger part of the monthly costs than it used to be, and that can feel like just one more thing to juggle when you’re buying a home or moving. But knowing you have ways to keep it in check can take some of the pressure off. Compare a few options before you buy, revisit your policy each year, and lean on trusted local professionals as you plan for your next move.

#5634. Google DeepMind releases new advanced robotics AI model and next-generation gene prediction model

Alphabet Inc.’s artificial intelligence research lab, Google DeepMind, Tuesday debuted the next generation of Gemini Robotics, the company’s most capable vision-language-action model to date for creating an “AI brain” for robotics.

Separately, DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 today, a next-generation AI model that can predict how DNA sequences and their variations affect human cell types, creating a powerful biological tool for fighting disease and drug development.

DeepMind said Gemini Robotics 2.5 enhances dexterity, reliability and safety to help engineers bring robots out of the lab and into dynamic, unstructured, real-world environments where they can coordinate alongside humans.

The company said that with the release of Gemini 4 Argon, the research division has been able to accelerate robot research and reach into physical AI. The new robotics AI model was tested across over 200 distinct tasks and the company said it anticipates scaling even further.

Argon, the company’s frontier artificial intelligence large language model, rolled out in late September, bringing advanced reasoning to the enterprise. Using the capabilities behind this new, flagship model, DeepMind said it allowed Gemini Robotics 2.5 to increase the breadth and speed with which robots can learn new skills and apply them to real-world scenarios.

The 2.5 version makes a significant jump in optimization and performance across three key areas. Boosted dexterity means robots running on 2.5 can perform more tasks with greater accuracy, including using everyday tools to handle delicate, flexible objects. With increased reliability, the new model successfully packed automotive parts with a 96% success rate during real-world proof-of-concept tests at Mercedes-Benz. Finally, DeepMind enhanced safety with improved physical steerability and introduced a new benchmark for testing against jailbreaks.

In evaluations, Robotics 2.5 now achieves a 30% to 100% success rate depending on the task and completes tasks 20% to 30% faster compared with the previous version’s baseline.

The company said that, like previous models, it natively works with many different types of robots, including Apptronik Inc.’s Apollo 2 humanoid robots and the Franka Duo platform with two-fingered parallel grippers.

“This is what we built Apollo for: useful work alongside people in real industrial settings,” Apptronik co-founder and Chief Executive Jeff Cardenas said. “Pairing Apollo 2 with Gemini Robotics, we saw the models improve dramatically in just a few weeks of post-training and carry over to Mercedes-Benz production with very little drop-off.”

Gemini Robotics 2.5 is rolling out today via DeepMind’s robotics partners, including Agile Robots SE, Apptronik and Boston Dynamics Inc.

AI models such as AlphaGenome help drug development and biotechnology companies turn genetic data into testable leads. By predicting how DNA changes affect gene activity and which cells in the body those changes act in, they can guide researchers to promising drug targets and help prioritize experiments.

Announced today, AlphaGenome 2 adds finer detail about specific cell types and states, potentially revealing disease-related effects that broader tissue-level models miss. These predictions guide research rather than replace experimental validation; the model is not approved for clinical or diagnostic use.

The problem researchers face is that every cell in the body carries the same DNA; however, different genes are activated at different times to differentiate cells and adjust their behavior. For example, a heart muscle cell or an immune cell fighting an infection may have the same DNA, but they use the blueprint to produce different proteins, enzymes and other tools to do their job.

DeepMind used global efforts from the Human Cell Atlas, a scientific consortium that mapped gene expression in millions of cells, to give the world an unprecedented view of how different cells use genes. However, predicting the paths and variations that drive activation and expression changes remains a major challenge.

Professor Sarah Teichmann, co-founder of the Human Cell Atlas and professor of Stem Cell Medicine at the University of Cambridge, said what makes Alphagenome 2 so powerful is “how it adapts directly to new single-cell data without retraining, predicting how DNA variants act in newly profiled cell states,” and that it can adapt even from very small samples.

According to DeepMind, the new model can predict core experimental readouts of DNA function as the previous generation, including gene expression, histone modification and chromatin accessibility – but also adds DNA methylation, which is a significant part of epigenetics, which explains how behaviors, environment and life experiences can influence gene activity.

#5633. What Experts Forecast for Mortgage Rates and Home Prices in 2027

When it comes to housing, two of the biggest questions on everyone’s mind right now are:

And if you’re weighing whether to move in the next few months or wait until 2027, here’s what you should know.

When experts look ahead to 2027, they see a steady housing market. No wild swings. No big surprises. Just a calmer, more balanced market.

And steady makes planning a whole lot easier. Let’s break it down.

Lots of people are holding out for lower rates. But the latest forecasts from Fannie Mae, the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA), and Wells Fargo show rates holding fairly flat through 2027 (see graph below):

Lenders see it the same way. In a recent survey from HousingWire, 70% of mortgage executives said they expect rates to be around 7.5% or higher six months from now (see graph below):

And if you’re wondering why, the answer is fairly simple. Chen Zhao, Head of Economics Research at Redfin, says:

“Until the underlying economic fundamentals—everything from oil prices to AI–that are keeping rates high change, mortgage rates are unlikely to fall significantly.”

So what does that mean for you? Instead of trying to guess where rates go next, focus on what you can control. Even if rates don’t budge, there are still ways to get the best rate possible. When you talk with your lender, ask about:

Your credit score. Even a small bump in your score could help lower your rate.

Different loan types. Some programs offer lower rates or smaller down payments than you might expect.

Buying down your rate. Paying a little more upfront (called “points”) can lower your rate and your monthly payment.

That way, you’ll know exactly where you stand and what a comfortable monthly payment looks like for you.

But what about prices? Here’s where steady really works in your favor.

Experts don’t see a home price drop coming. On average, forecasts from Fannie Mae, MBA, and Wells Fargo show prices rising about 1% to 1.5% a year through 2027 (see graph below):

In plain terms, in most places prices are still going up, just not as fast. For sellers, that means your home should hold onto its value. For buyers, slower growth gives you a little more breathing room. Just don’t count on prices getting cheaper while you wait.

But keep in mind, these are national forecasts. Prices can look very different from one area to the next, so what matters most is what’s happening where you live.

When the market is steady, you don’t have to try to time it perfectly. There’s no big swing to wait out.

That puts the focus back on you. Maybe you need more space for a growing family. Maybe you’re ready for less upkeep. A steady market makes it easier to plan for either one.

If you’re asking yourself should you move now or wait? You should know experts see a steady market through 2027, with rates holding near today’s levels and prices rising slowly. So, rather than waiting for a big shift that may not come, connect with a local real estate agent and run the numbers on what a move looks like at today’s rates and prices, so you can decide based on your goals instead of the headlines.

#5632. Kim Kardashian’s Former Beverly Hills Tuscan Villa From Early Seasons of ‘Keeping Up With the Kardashians’ Hits the Market for $8.5 Million

Kim Kardashian’s former Beverly Hills home has hit the market, with an asking price of $8.495 million for a piece of reality television history.

The five-bedroom, five-bathroom home was featured heavily in the earliest seasons of “Keeping Up With the Kardashians.” Remember when Kris Jenner and Khloé Kardashian went out on the town, and after a few too many margaritas, decided to toilet-paper the Tuscan-style villa?

Fortunately, the defaced rose bushes have been cleaned up since that 2013 episode.

Kim purchased the 4,027-square-foot home for $3.4 million in 2010. Three years later, she sold it fully-furnished, and it went for $5.12 million after a bidding war, according to Robb Report.

Later, in 2024, Kim visited the property with Khloé and celebrity broker Josh Altman, to find that it was still nearly exactly as she’d left it. Recognizable details such as a “KK” logo on the wall of her iconic glam room and her custom bedding were still there, prompting the star to share a tour of the time capsule on her Snapchat profile.

Today, the famous family’s connection to the estate is more of an “if you know, you know” situation. It’s undergone a complete transformation by AD100 designer Sebastian Zuchowicki, and now boasts a more sleek, contemporary look.

With that said, many of the structural features that made the home a gem in the first place are still present.

The gourmet kitchen has been redone in a European country style, with custom cabinetry and a spacious center island. Charming windows line one wall, while a double-sided fireplace connects the breakfast room and lounge. New, top-of-the-line appliances have also been added.

The primary suite is certainly luxurious, with a fireside seating area, two fabulous and generously-sized walk-in closets, and a spa-inspired Italian-tiled bathroom that features double vanities, a soothing shower, and a unique soaking tub.

Additionally, the second floor also includes three more en suite bedrooms, which each have a distinct personality. From floral wallpaper to chic striped walls, these rooms manage to be neutral and statement-making at the same time.

The home is perfectly primed for entertaining, especially considering the private theater.

Indoor-outdoor living is encouraged, with a covered fireplace lounge and a fully equipped outdoor kitchen.

The resort-style pool and spa makes the backyard feel like a true getaway. There’s also a tranquil fountain, a hillside sun terrace, a dedicated bathroom, and a fire pit. A gazebo and cabana serves as a spot to watch television without being cooped up inside.

The gourmet kitchen is appointed with custom cabinetry, premium appliances, a spacious center island, and a double-sided fireplace connecting the breakfast room and lounge. A private theater provides an additional space for entertainment.

Today, Kim holds an impressive collection of properties in California and Idaho. Most notably, she’s spent years renovating her $60 million Hidden Hills home. The home has been undergoing major construction since 2024, and during a recent episode of “The Kardashians,” it was revealed that the Skims founder is creating an 8,000-square-foot closet.

Kim continues to share her real estate updates with viewers, and during the Nov. 5 episode of the family’s Hulu show, she purchased a new Palm Springs, CA, estate on what appeared to be a whim.

The Kardashian-Jenners have a series of homes in La Quinta, with hidden pathways connecting the properties. When Kim realized the house located next door to Kylie Jenner’s abode was up for grabs, she sneaked onto the property to see if she liked it better than her existing home.

Later in the episode, Khloé confirmed that her older sister had, in fact, made the purchase.
